result.title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
result.summary: Manim supports precise, programmatic video generation, but a successfully rendered educational animation can still have visual defects, missing explanations, or incorrect content. Rendering does not directly identify the code changes needed to correct these visual failures, so feedback-driven revision is needed. Existing agentic frameworks use iterative rendering and revision but typically rely on large models, often proprietary. Existing Manim datasets primarily contain final programs and often lack quality verification and the trajectories of feedback and revisions needed to learn this refinement process. We introduce ManimData and ManimCode, a data and training framework for feedback-driven educational animation generation. We construct ManimData through a render-guided pipeline that iteratively generates, executes, reviews, and revises Manim programs with retrieved API documentation. Its 24,034 render-verified, quality-filtered records preserve intermediate programs, execution errors, visual critiques, and corrective revisions. We use role-conditioned supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories to train ManimCode, a single 4B model, to write, review, and revise animation programs. To improve correction of errors that differ from those in the collected trajectories, we then train the Reviser with reinforcement learning on self-generated states, using rendering outcomes and reference-free quality feedback. ManimCode achieves 96.6% and 97.0% render success on ManimData-test and ManimBench, compared with 52.6% and 82.0% for the untrained 4B model under the same inference setup, while also improving video quality scores from 2.48 to 2.94 and from 3.00 to 3.44. Integrating ManimCode into two long-form educational video generation systems increases completed videos from 19/117 to 107/117 and from 53/239 to 239/239, alongside improvements in educational effectiveness and visual quality.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ManimData 数据集与 ManimCode 训练框架，用「生成—执行渲染—视觉评审—修订」轨迹做角色条件监督微调，再用渲染结果与无参考质量反馈对 Reviser 做强化学习，使 4B 模型学会写作、审查和修订教育动画程序。
AI.relevance_reason: 渲染结果与视觉评审作为外部证据驱动多轮修订，其轨迹监督与在自生成状态上训练 Reviser 的做法，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选、修订收益分配与何时停止迭代提供可核查线索，但本身不涉及模型内部 latent 推理状态。
